Is the two party system coming to an end?

No. The game theory of first past the post ensures that there will always be a two party system. To have multiple parties you need the single transferrable vote.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s7tWHJfhiyo

This guy does a good job of explaining each of these voting systems and their benefits/drawbacks.

TL;DW - First past the post means majority vote wins (what we currently have), and statistically ALWAYS results in 2 choices. Single transferable vote means that you rank the candidates in the order you like, so voting for the person you want doesn't "spoil" the person you want second (who is running a similar platform).

It's just a different polling method.

  • On your ballot paper you list candidates in order of preference, like "Supreme 1, Johnson 2, Trump 3, Clinton 4, Sanders 5" or whatever, up to 10 places.

  • Then when the votes are collected, all the first preferences are checked during the first count. At this point, the lowest scoring candidates who have no chance of winning are eliminated, so Vermin Supreme would be gone.

  • Then they count all the votes again, but this time, anyone who had a first preference for Vermin Supreme, they'll read his second preference instead. So my vote will transfer to Gary Johnson.

  • If Johnson is eliminated and there's still no clear winner, they go to a third count, and my vote will transfer to trump. And so on and so forth.

The idea is that you can make a risky vote for a third party, but still have your vote count for something if that person doesn't get elected. It also means third parties don't end up splitting the dem or republican vote, if they don't get elected, then all of their votes will revert to other candidates as if they hadn't run.
